literal: Xin Shu; Yuan Wenyao; Zhao Yanshen
idiomatic: Xin Shu; Yuan Wenyao; Zhao Yanshen

literal: Xin Shu, styled Huaizhe, from youth was bright and keen, with judgment and discernment.
idiomatic: Xin Shu, styled Huaizhe, was clever and perceptive from boyhood, with a steady sense of what mattered.

literal: Upon first office he was Staff Member in the Registrar's Office of the Directorate of Works; together with Vice Director Gao Longzhi he oversaw the construction of Ye's palaces—Shu had thoughtful designs, and all the crafts were brought to completion.
idiomatic: His first appointment was staff member in the registrar's office of the directorate of works; with vice director Gao Longzhi he directed the building of Ye's palaces. Shu planned well, and every trade met its mark.

literal: He was promoted again to Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was promoted again to right vice director of the masters of writing.

literal: Sent out as Administrator of Qinghe; his governance won a reputation for ability.
idiomatic: Sent out as administrator of Qinghe, he earned a name for capable rule.

literal: Retroactively appointed Chief Clerk of Bing province; he left office on father's mourning.
idiomatic: He was retroactively made chief clerk of Bing province, then left office to mourn his father.

literal: Several hundred elders of Qinghe went to the capital to request a stele praising his virtue.
idiomatic: Several hundred Qinghe elders went to court to ask that a stele be raised in praise of his virtue.

literal: When Gao Cheng took up the succession, together with Left Vice Director Song Youdao, Secretariat Attendant Li Hui, and others he hurried to Jinyang; all became honored guests.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng assumed power, he went with left vice director Song Youdao, secretariat attendant Li Hui, and others to Jinyang and was received as an honored guest.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry.
idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to regular attendant of the scattered cavalry.

literal: In the eighth year of Wuding, Hou Jing rebelled; Shu was appointed Masters of Writing on the Southeastern Circuit Mobile Grand Secretariat, enfeoffed as Marquis of Jiangxia county (male), and with Gao Yue and others defeated Hou Jing and captured Xiao Ming.
idiomatic: In the eighth year of Wuding, Hou Jing rebelled. Shu was made masters of writing on the southeastern mobile grand secretariat and enfeoffed as marquis of Jiangxia. With Gao Yue and others he broke Hou Jing and took Xiao Ming prisoner.

literal: Transferred to Governor of Eastern Xuzhou; made Commissioner for the Pacification of Huainan.
idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Eastern Xuzhou and made commissioner for Huainan pacification.

literal: In the first year of Tianbao of Qi, Hou Jing levied rents and taxes from Jiangxi; Shu led the armies across the Huai to cut it off and burned several million shi of his rice.
idiomatic: In Qi's first Tianbao year, Hou Jing levied rents from Jiangxi. Shu led troops across the Huai to block him and burned several million shi of his grain.

literal: Returning to garrison at Xiapi, more than three thousand households followed Shu north across the Huai.
idiomatic: When he returned to garrison Xiapi, more than three thousand households followed him north across the Huai.

literal: Guo Zhi, Governor of Eastern Xuzhou, killed the commandery administrator.
idiomatic: Guo Zhi, governor of Eastern Xuzhou, killed his commandery administrator.

literal: Gao Yang heard of it and ordered Shu: from now on in the more than ten provinces under his command, wherever anyone violated the law, the governor should first report and await instruction; subordinates might judge first and memorialize afterward.
idiomatic: Gao Yang heard of it and ordered Shu that in the dozen-odd provinces under him, whenever anyone broke the law the governor must first report and wait for word; lower officials might decide first and memorialize later.

literal: In Qi, a mobile grand secretariat concurrently overseeing personnel matters began with Shu.
idiomatic: In Qi the practice of a mobile grand secretariat also holding personnel authority began with Shu.

literal: The Governor of Anzhou, Administrator of Linqing, and the two garrison commanders of Xuyi and Qicheng all violated capital crimes; Shu investigated, memorialized, and had them executed.
idiomatic: The governor of Anzhou, the administrator of Linqing, and the garrison commanders of Xuyi and Qicheng all committed capital crimes; Shu investigated, memorialized, and had them put to death.

literal: The Governor of Suizhou and all the commandery administrators under him committed capital offenses; the court granted Shu all their hundred-odd slaves and entire assets; he declined three times but was not permitted; Shu then sent them to the relevant office and no longer kept them for himself.
idiomatic: The governor of Suizhou and every commandery administrator under him faced capital punishment. The court granted Shu all their slaves—more than a hundred households—and their property. He declined three times and was refused; Shu then turned everything over to the proper office and did not keep it.

literal: Xing Shao heard of it and sent Shu a letter, saying: "In antiquity Zhongli Yi said, 'Confucius bore thirst at Robber Spring,' and thereby cast pearls and jades to the ground; you, sir, can do the same today—one may call it the same moment across different ages.
idiomatic: Xing Shao heard and wrote Shu: "Long ago Zhongli Yi said that Confucius would endure thirst rather than drink from Robber Spring, and so cast pearls and jade aside; you, sir, can do as much today—truly one moment in another age.

literal: " When Wang Sengbian defeated Hou Jing, Shu recruited and pacified; cities and garrisons in succession submitted; in all more than twenty provinces.
idiomatic: " When Wang Sengbian defeated Hou Jing, Shu won men over and pacified the land; towns and garrisons submitted one after another—more than twenty provinces in all.

literal: Thereupon he moved his command to Guangling.
idiomatic: He then shifted his headquarters to Guangling.

literal: He obtained the dynastic seal and sent it to Ye; Gao Yang reported the seal at the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
idiomatic: He recovered the dynastic seal and sent it to Ye; Gao Yang presented it at the imperial ancestral temple.

literal: This seal was that made by Qin, four inches square, with a knob of interlaced dragons; its inscription read: "Ordered by Heaven; long life and eternal prosperity.
idiomatic: This was the seal Qin had made: four inches square, with a knob of interlaced dragons. Its inscription read, "Ordered by Heaven; long life and eternal prosperity.

literal: " The Two Han transmitted it; it was also transmitted through Wei and Jin.
idiomatic: " The two Han dynasties passed it down; Wei and Jin passed it down as well.

literal: When Emperor Huai was defeated, it was lost among Liu Cong.
idiomatic: When Emperor Huai was defeated, it was lost to Liu Cong.

literal: When Cong was defeated, it was lost among the Shi clan.
idiomatic: When Cong fell, it passed to the Shi clan.

literal: When the Shi clan was defeated, in the Yonghe era of Emperor Mu of Jin, Dai Sengshi, Administrator of Puyang, obtained it and sent Supervisor He Rong to deliver it to Jiankang.
idiomatic: When the Shi fell, in the Yonghe reign of Jin's Emperor Mu, Dai Sengshi, administrator of Puyang, obtained it and sent supervisor He Rong to deliver it to Jiankang.

literal: It passed through Song, Qi, and Liang; when Liang fell, Hou Jing obtained it.
idiomatic: It passed through Song, Qi, and Liang; when Liang fell, Hou Jing took it.

literal: When Jing was defeated, Attendant Zhong Zhao Sixian cast the seal upon Jing's Southern Yanzhou Governor Guo Yuanjian, who sent it to Shu; therefore Shu presented it.
idiomatic: When Jing was defeated, attendant-in-ordinary Zhao Sixian gave the seal to Jing's southern Yanzhou governor Guo Yuanjian, who sent it to Shu; thus Shu was able to present it.

literal: Soon summoned as Masters of Writing in the Palace, leading Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and still deliberated on laws and ordinances with court worthies.
idiomatic: He was soon summoned as palace masters of writing and director of the imperial ancestral temple, and still joined court worthies in revising laws and ordinances.

literal: Promoted to Director of Personnel; drew salary as titular chief of Liang commandery in Southern Yanzhou.
idiomatic: He was promoted to director of personnel and drew salary as titular chief of Liang commandery in southern Yanzhou.

literal: After the move to Ye, the great selection posts had four well-known holders, each with gain and loss, none attaining perfection.
idiomatic: After the court moved to Ye, four famous men held the great selection office in turn; each had strengths and flaws, and none achieved perfection.

literal: Gao Cheng in his youth was lofty and clear; what harmed him was laxity.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng in his youth was bright and open; his fault was looseness.

literal: Yuan Shude was deep, close, and cautious; what harmed him was minuteness.
idiomatic: Yuan Shude was grave, careful, and thorough; his fault was excessive detail.

literal: Yang Yin was polished and quick in debate; in selecting men he erred toward flashiness.
idiomatic: Yang Yin was eloquent and quick; in choosing men he favored show over substance.

literal: Only Shu, by nature upright and clear, chose men by talent and capacity, held names to facts, mixed old and new in nomination, must promote from storehouses, and did not leave out noble houses.
idiomatic: Only Shu, upright by nature, chose by talent and office, matched names to reality, mixed veterans and newcomers, promoted men from the storehouses, and did not overlook great families.

literal: Reviewing selection before and after, Shu's was most balanced, and was greatly praised by the age.
idiomatic: Comparing earlier and later rounds of selection, Shu's was the most even-handed, and his age praised him highly.

literal: Late in Tianbao, Gao Yang once had Shu select a hundred officials; those who competed numbered two or three thousand; Shu examined the scholars; none slandered; those he honored and promoted later all attained high prominence.
idiomatic: Late in Tianbao, Gao Yang once ordered Shu to choose a hundred officials from two or three thousand candidates. Shu tested the scholars; no one murmured against him, and those he advanced later all rose to high rank.

literal: Shu was pure and frugal, with few desires.
idiomatic: Shu was austere and frugal, with few wants.

literal: Diligent in his duties, never briefly slackening.
idiomatic: He was diligent in office and never slackened even for a moment.

literal: Facing armies with stern authority; governing the people with beneficent policy.
idiomatic: Before the army he was stern; over the people he ruled with kindness.

literal: In youth he loved literature and history; in later years he studied further; though on campaign, his hand never left the scroll.
idiomatic: He loved letters in youth and studied harder in later years; even on campaign he never put down his books.

literal: When Huainan was pacified, of all goods he touched not a hairsbreadth; he only gathered books in great number—mostly fine editions from Song, Qi, and Liang times—more than ten thousand scrolls collected, together with famous paintings by Gu and Lu and their school, and calligraphies after the Two Wangs in no small number; none went to the imperial storehouse—only into his private gate.
idiomatic: When Huainan was settled he took not a thread of booty, but gathered books in force—mostly fine Song, Qi, and Liang editions, more than ten thousand scrolls—along with celebrated paintings by Gu, Lu, and their circle and many works of calligraphy after the Two Wangs. None went to the imperial treasury; all entered his private house.

literal: When he returned to court, he often gifted powerful figures; public opinion thereby thought less of him.
idiomatic: On returning to court he often sent gifts to the powerful, and opinion thought less of him for it.

literal: In the tenth year he died, age sixty.
idiomatic: He died in the tenth year, at sixty.

literal: In the second year of Huangjian, posthumously granted Grand Mentor with ceremonies equal to the Three Excellencies, Supervisor of the Secretariat, Governor of Qingzhou.
idiomatic: In the second year of Huangjian he was posthumously made grand mentor with ceremonies equal to the three excellencies, supervisor of the secretariat, and governor of Qingzhou.

literal: His son Geqing was a Masters of Writing lang.
idiomatic: His son Geqing served as a masters of writing lang.

literal: Geqing's younger brother Hengqing had judgment and learning; staff member in a grand mentor's office.
idiomatic: Geqing's younger brother Hengqing was learned and discerning and served as staff in a grand mentor's office.

literal: Early in Daye of Sui, he died as Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
idiomatic: Early in Sui's Daye reign he died as vice director of the imperial ancestral temple.

literal: Yuan Wenyao, styled Deyuan, a man of Luoyang in Henan; sixth-generation descendant of Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei.
idiomatic: Yuan Wenyao, styled Deyuan, was from Luoyang in Henan commandery, a sixth-generation descendant of Emperor Zhaocheng of Wei.

literal: His fifth-generation ancestor was Prince Changshan, Zun.
idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor was Prince Changshan, Zun.

literal: His father Xi had filial conduct; when his father died, he dwelt by the tomb until he died himself.
idiomatic: His father Xi was famed for filial piety; when his own father died, he lived by the tomb until he died there.

literal: When Wenyao rose high, Xi was posthumously granted Special Advancement, Grand Mentor equal to Three Excellencies, Supervisor of Secretariat, posthumous name Xiao (Filial).
idiomatic: When Wenyao rose high, Xi was posthumously made special advancement, grand mentor equal to the three excellencies, and supervisor of the secretariat, with the posthumous name Filial.

literal: Wenyao from youth was keen and clever; Prince of Jiyin Huiye often said: "This boy is talent for assisting a king.
idiomatic: Wenyao was clever from childhood. The prince of Jiyin, Huiye, often said, "This child has the makings of a king's helper.

literal: " Huiye once gathered guests in great assembly; someone brought the Collected Works of He Xun newly into Luoyang; all the worthies praised it.
idiomatic: " Once Huiye held a great gathering of guests. Someone brought He Xun's collected works, newly arrived in Luoyang, and every worthy present praised them.

literal: Xing Shao of Hejian tested Wenyao: "Recite it—how many times through before you can?
idiomatic: Xing Shao of Hejian tested Wenyao: "Recite it—how many readings before you can?

literal: " Wenyao read once and recited; he was then just over ten.
idiomatic: " Wenyao read it once and recited it; he was barely past ten.

literal: The Prince of Jiyin said: "My house's thousand-li colt—what is he now?
idiomatic: The prince of Jiyin said, "My house's thousand-li colt—what has he become?

literal: " Xing said: "This is probably without precedent since antiquity."
idiomatic: " Xing said, "This is probably unmatched since antiquity."

literal: His first office was Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, outside the regular quota.
idiomatic: He began office as regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, outside the regular quota.

literal: He suffered father's mourning; when mourning ended, made Libationer in the Eastern Pavilion of the Grand Marshal.
idiomatic: After his father's death and mourning, he was made libationer in the eastern pavilion of the grand marshal.

literal: As the realm was in turmoil, he resigned office to tend his mother and hid on Mount Linlü.
idiomatic: With the realm in turmoil, he resigned to care for his mother and lived in seclusion on Mount Linlü.

literal: In Wuding, Gao Cheng summoned him as Staff Officer of the Grand General's government office.
idiomatic: In the Wuding era Gao Cheng summoned him as staff officer in the grand general's office.

literal: When Qi received the mandate, at the altar of enthronement he received the post of Secretariat Drafting Officer, proclaiming civil and military orders.
idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate, at the enthronement altar he was made secretariat drafting officer and proclaimed civil and military orders.

literal: Yang Zunyian often said: "He who can take the Marquis of Rang's seal must be this man.
idiomatic: Yang Zunyian often said, "The man who can take the Marquis of Rang's seal must be this one.

literal: " Later he was suddenly imprisoned by secret imperial order, and in the end none knew the reason.
idiomatic: " Later he was suddenly seized on a secret imperial order; in the end no one knew why.

literal: Thus for many years.
idiomatic: He remained so for many years.

literal: Later Gao Yang himself visited the prison, took his hand in ashamed apology, personally removed his gold belt and imperial robes and bestowed them, and that same day raised him to Lang in the Sacrificial Affairs section of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Later Gao Yang himself visited the prison, took his hand in apology, removed his own gold belt and court robes to give him, and that same day made him lang in the sacrificial affairs section of the masters of writing.

literal: When Gao Yan acted as regent, appointed Staff Officer in the Grand Chancellor's government office, overseeing secrets.
idiomatic: When Gao Yan acted as regent, Wenyao was made staff officer in the grand chancellor's office and handled confidential matters.

literal: When he ascended the throne, made Secretariat Attendant, enfeoffed as Baron of Yongle county, and deliberated on great affairs of state.
idiomatic: When Gao Yan took the throne, Wenyao was made secretariat attendant, enfeoffed as baron of Yongle county, and took part in great affairs of state.

literal: When the emperor was gravely ill, together with Prince of Pingyuan Guiyan, Prince of Zhao Jun Rui, and others he received final charge and welcomed Gao Zhan to the throne.
idiomatic: When the emperor was near death, he and Prince of Pingyuan Guiyan, Prince of Zhao Jun Rui, and others received the final charge and installed Gao Zhan.

literal: Upon enthronement his favor grew ever higher; he passed through Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, Chamberlain for Attendants, Supervisor of Secretariat.
idiomatic: After Gao Zhan took the throne, Wenyao's favor rose still higher. He served in turn as attendant-in-ordinary of the yellow gate, regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, chamberlain for attendants, and supervisor of the secretariat.

literal: In the second year of Tiantong, an edict specially granted the surname Gao; registration placed under the Director of Imperial Clan; sons and younger brothers per regulation attended court at the seasons.
idiomatic: In the second year of Tiantong an edict specially granted him the surname Gao, registered him with the director of the imperial clan, and allowed his sons and younger brothers to attend seasonal court audiences by regulation.

literal: Promoted again to Left Vice Director of Masters of Writing; advanced to Duke of Ningdu commandery, still chamberlain for attendants.
idiomatic: He was promoted again to left vice director of the masters of writing and advanced to duke of Ningdu commandery while retaining the post of chamberlain for attendants.

literal: Wenyao served three sovereigns, clear in worldly affairs; whenever he faced the throne he was often ordered to proclaim edicts; his civil and military orders rang high and clear, delivered without hindrance.
idiomatic: Wenyao served three sovereigns and knew the affairs of the age. Whenever he faced the throne he was often ordered to proclaim edicts; his voice rang clear, and he delivered civil and military orders without stumbling.

literal: Yet probing the sovereign's intent, he sometimes had alley language, and so was not greatly valued by those who understood.
idiomatic: Yet in reading the sovereign's mind he sometimes used coarse speech, and men of discernment did not esteem him highly.

literal: Qi inherited Wei; county magistrates were often base appointees, until gentlemen would be ashamed to hold a hundred-li post.
idiomatic: Qi followed Wei in making county magistrates too often from lowborn men, until gentlemen were ashamed to govern a hundred-li district.

literal: Wenyao held that the magistrate was crucial to caring for the people, and so requested reform of selection.
idiomatic: Wenyao held that the magistrate was the hinge of caring for the people and asked to reform how they were chosen.

literal: Thereupon secret orders searched out noble scions; edicts issued to employ them.
idiomatic: Secret orders then sought out sons of great houses, and edicts put them in office.

literal: Still fearing their appeals and complaints, all were summoned at the Shenwu Gate; Prince of Zhao Jun Rui was ordered to proclaim names and offer words of thick consolation.
idiomatic: Still fearing they would appeal, he gathered them all at Shenwu Gate and had Prince of Zhao Jun Rui read the edict, call each name, and speak words of comfort.

literal: Gentlemen serving as county magistrates began from this.
idiomatic: From this gentlemen began to serve as county magistrates.

literal: As he shared favor with Zhao Yanshen and He Shikai, though he was not like Yanshen in purity and holding the Way, nor like Shikai in greedy debauchery and disordering government, he stood between the second and third.
idiomatic: He shared favor with Zhao Yanshen and He Shikai. He was not so pure and steadfast as Yanshen, nor so greedy and corrupt as Shikai, but stood between them.

literal: Yet his nature was genial and thick, without contention with others, and so contemporary opinion did not rank him below Yanshen.
idiomatic: Yet he was mild and easy by nature and did not contend with others, and opinion did not place him below Yanshen.

literal: At first, when Wenyao moved from Luoyang to Ye, he had only ten qing of land; the family was poor—enough only for food and clothing.
idiomatic: When Wenyao first moved from Luoyang to Ye he had only ten qing of land; the household was poor and had barely enough to eat and wear.

literal: As Wei neared its end, clan names were insulted; someone falsely seized and encroached; Wenyao at once yielded it to him.
idiomatic: As Wei neared its fall, clan members were bullied. Someone seized his land by force; Wenyao at once yielded it.

literal: When he rose high, that man was still alive and fled with his household.
idiomatic: When Wenyao rose high, that man was still alive and fled with his family.

literal: Wenyao was greatly alarmed, pursued him with comfort, and again yielded it.
idiomatic: Wenyao was alarmed, sent after him with reassurances, and again offered him the land.

literal: The other man was ashamed and would not accept; each yielded to the other, and it became idle land.
idiomatic: The man was ashamed and would not take it; each insisted on yielding, and the field lay fallow.

literal: When the Later Sovereign succeeded, Prince Zhao Jun Rui, Lou Dingyuan, and others plotted to remove He Shikai; Wenyao also joined the deliberation.
idiomatic: When the Later Sovereign succeeded, Prince of Zhao Jun Rui, Lou Dingyuan, and others plotted to remove He Shikai; Wenyao joined the plot.

literal: Rui was killed; Wenyao thereby went out as Governor of Western Yanzhou.
idiomatic: Rui was killed, and Wenyao was sent out as governor of western Yanzhou.

literal: Taking leave of Shikai, Shikai said: "The post you received is fair ground; to make a Yuan-family lad chancellor-in-chief deeply shames the court.
idiomatic: When he took leave of Shikai, Shikai said, "You have been given a post that speaks for itself; to make a Yuan boy chancellor and vice chancellor is a deep shame to the court.

literal: " Having spoken, he regretted it and still took Wenyao's hand in consolation.
idiomatic: " Having said it, he regretted his words and still took Wenyao's hand in consolation.

literal: Still fearing Wenyao's self-doubt, he employed his son Xinggong as Masters of Writing lang to comfort his heart.
idiomatic: Still fearing Wenyao would doubt him, he appointed Wenyao's son Xinggong as a masters of writing lang to set his mind at ease.

literal: When Shikai died, summoned from Governor of Eastern Xuzhou to court, he was ultimately not employed and died.
idiomatic: After Shikai died he was summoned from governor of Eastern Xuzhou to court, but was never used and died.

literal: Xinggong had beautiful appearance, his father's manner, and moreover brilliant talent; he reached Secretariat Drafting Officer, awaiting edicts at the Wenlin Hall.
idiomatic: Xinggong was handsome, had his father's bearing, and was gifted besides. He reached secretariat drafting officer and awaited edicts at the Wenlin Hall.

literal: When Qi perished, Yang Xiuzhi and eighteen others entered the passes together; he was gradually promoted to Lower Grand Master in the Bureau of Merits.
idiomatic: When Qi fell, Yang Xiuzhi and eighteen others entered the passes together with him. He rose gradually to lower grand master in the bureau of merits.

literal: In Kaihuang of Sui he reached Masters of Writing lang; on account of offense he was banished to Guazhou and died.
idiomatic: Under Sui's Kaihuang reign he became a masters of writing lang; for an offense he was banished to Guazhou and died there.

literal: Xinggong in youth was rather proud and self-willed; Wenyao had him associate with Lu Sidao of Fanyang.
idiomatic: Xinggong was rather proud in youth; Wenyao had him keep company with Lu Sidao of Fanyang.

literal: Wenyao once told Sidao: "The boy lately knows a little—this is elder brother's doing; yet his white-dice gambling and heavy drinking very much take the master's style.
idiomatic: Wenyao once told Sidao, "The boy has learned a little lately—your doing as elder brother; but his dice-playing and hard drinking are very much in your master's style.

literal: " Sidao answered: "Your son's rhetoric is lofty and sharp—he can surely bear the hall's beam; yet white-dice gambling and heavy drinking are also gifts of nature."
idiomatic: " Sidao answered, "Your son's eloquence is sharp and lofty—he can surely uphold the family hall; but dice and deep cups are also his nature."
